newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil mixed and quiet at close.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil mixed and quiet at close.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices remained mixed at the close of business on Thursday in a quiet market.
Soft oils showed no sign of a rally despite higher Chicago soy oil futures in early trade.
"People are not keen to sell the market down, but on the other hand they don't seem to want to follow the higher opening in Chicago," said one trader.
In the palm oil market news that Egypt had bought at its tender gave the market some support, but traders said the prices paid were not good for the market.

European traders reported at first that Egypt had bought 20,000 tonnes of palm oil, but later Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries said it had bought a total of 25,000 tonnes of palm oil.
It bought 15,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil, not 10,000 tonnes, but confirmed the price at $534.50 c and F. It also bought 10,000 tonnes of palm stearin at $404 a tonne all from FELDA.
European traders said the oil was for arrival in July.
At the close of business crude palm oil cif Europe was $5 up after Jun traded at $540 a tonne cif.
Products closed unchanged to $2.50 up after stearin fetched $375 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for Jul.
Coconut oil finished $5 up to unchanged after Aug/Sep traded at 4625 A tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil closed unchanged to $2.50 lower.
Dutch soy oil ended two to one guilders lower after Jul trade at 104.75 and 105 guilders, Aug/Oct at 104.50 and 104 and Nov/Jan at 103.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Rape oil was 1.50 to one guilders lower after Aug/Oct traded at 103.25 and Nov/Jan at 104.00 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8062
